headline: Isomorphic Labs, the drug-discovery spin-off of Google DeepMind, is reportedly in early talks to raise money at a value of at least $40 billion.
score_reason: Kept at pool score 7: a very large reported valuation, but early talks that could change.
importance_line: What changed is how much investors are reportedly willing to pay for AI drug discovery, which could matter to patients if it speeds up new medicines but no AI-designed medicine has reached the market yet, then to pharma partners such as Eli Lilly and Novartis, and the doubt is that these are early talks reported by Bloomberg and the terms may change.
summary: Bloomberg reports, as relayed by Yahoo Finance Canada, that the London-based AI drug-discovery company is in early talks on new funding that would value it at $40 billion and possibly up to $50 billion, with terms that could change before any deal closes. It would be a sharp rise from five months ago, when it raised $2.1 billion in a Series B round (a mid-stage investment round) backed substantially by Alphabet.
notes: Bloomberg is the first reporter; the text was read on the Yahoo Finance Canada copy, whose link is given because the Bloomberg link is not available.
